terms.comment: “Few” and “a few” alike: paucīs diēbus, in a few days. As a noun, paucī are few people, a handful, and pauca a few words: Paucīs tē volō, “a quick word with you” (Ter. And. 29). The singular is very rare (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: few and far between, scattered; rare
evidence: Verg. A. 1.118: adpārent rārī nantēs in gurgite vastō
terms.comment: Few in the sense of thinly spread, here and there; also rare, uncommon.

phrases.latin: paucīs temeritās est bonō, multīs malō
phrases.english: rashness turns out well for a few, and badly for many

phrases.latin: Paucōrum est intellegere, quid dōnet diēs.
phrases.english: Few understand what the day is giving.

sources: Lewis & Short: paucus · Lewis & Short: rarus
